scope: Website materialization/seal-recovery integration only; no public bootstrap or mutation execution

findings.title: Refresh durable intent before admitting another tab after takeover
findings.scenario: Tab B is loaded while shared storage is empty. Tab A materializes/seals, stores pending intent and loses acknowledgement. After A detaches, B opens and prepares the same store. B still has intent=null and may materialize, mint a new request key/attempt and overwrite the original unresolved durable reference. Exclusive database ownership does not refresh B memory.
findings.minimalCorrection: Re-read/validate shared durable intent after open/prepare and immediately before preview/seal. Any retained intent or read error must block fresh work. Use storage events to update stale UI, plus an existing-second-tab takeover browser regression that preserves the original key/reference without a fresh seal dispatch.
findings.independentReproduction: page-controls-before-fix.json: 2 seal dispatches and unequal original/retained keys

nonblockingDocumentation: Worker line1 claims messages cannot supply SQL despite preview accepting source SQL for original compiler. README still says only open/register/close. Update to describe actual closed command surface and fixed host model.
limitations: Independent page/worker controls use explicit synthetic DOM/storage/Worker/provider adapters in Bun, not PGlite or browser native execution.

Actual retained parent Chromium evidence is current for its zero-row, quota-before-dispatch and dropped-acknowledgement/reload cases; it does not yet cover the reproduced stale existing second-tab takeover.
Native execution, data bootstrap and full end-to-end mutation remain unqualified.
